candidates.summary: Object.typ comes from the caller's static pointer type, not the object, so one object yields unequal Objects and a caller-chosen Type()
candidates.failure_scenario: p := &Token{} persisted; Of(p) and Of((*Alias)(p)) (type Alias Token), or Of(b) and Of((*Mine)(b)) for b *strings.Builder and type Mine strings.Builder declared in another package, return the same id and address but typ Token vs Alias, so o1 == o2 is false, a map[reflect.Object] holds two entries for one object, and Type() reports whatever type the caller converted to. The Object doc promises 'Two Objects are equal if and only if they name the same object' and 'safe as a map key'; a realm deduplicating or keying balances by Object can be made to count one object twice by any caller that converts the pointer before handing it over. Deriving typ from hiv.Value.T is not a drop-in fix for a *interface pointee, whose dynamic type changes on assignment.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/b1-reach-conversion-splits-object.gno gnovm/tests/files/zrealm_reflect_conversion.gno && go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang -run 'TestFiles/zrealm_reflect_conversion.gno' -count=1: expect 'same object equal: true', observe false
candidates.evidence: go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang -run 'TestFiles/zrealm_reflect_conversion.gno' at 58b269206: +same object equal: false / +map entries for one object: 2 / +type via alias: gno.land/r/demo/reflectconv.Alias / +cross-package equal: false / +type via Mine: gno.land/r/demo/reflectconv.Mine. A gno test probe of the same shapes printed 'equal: false sameAddr: true' for both the in-package and cross-package conversion.

candidates.summary: PkgPath of a /p/ or stdlib package-level object names that package, not a realm, against its doc 'the path of the realm that created the object'
candidates.failure_scenario: Of(io.EOF) returns ok with PkgPath 'io'; Of(pager.ErrInvalidPageNumber) returns PkgPath 'gno.land/p/jeronimoalbi/pager/v0'; Of(strings.ToUpper) returns PkgPath 'strings'. These are stamped by the throwaway realm FinalizeRealmTransaction records for non-realm packages, so a caller treating PkgPath as a realm (deriving a refund address from it, matching it against realm paths) gets a library path; the doc on PkgPath and the package comment only describe realm-created objects.
candidates.verify_by: gno test a filetest printing reflect.Of(io.EOF).PkgPath() and reflect.Of(strings.ToUpper).PkgPath(): observed 'io' and 'strings'
